steps.say: Pancreatitis is sorted by whether the gland dies and whether organs fail. Brief failure with recovery sits in the middle, while failure that will not reverse marks the severe end needing intensive care.
steps.tx: **Revised Atlanta** (pancreatitis severity scheme) separates interstitial oedematous from **necrotising pancreatitis** (dying gland tissue), with organ failure under **48 hours** (two days) marking moderately severe and persistent failure marking severe disease with prolonged intensive care need and multi-organ support throughout.

steps.say: Stones and drink cause most attacks, but very high blood fats and calcium can trigger one alone. When stones are the culprit, the gallbladder comes out during the same admission once the storm passes.
steps.tx: Gallstones and alcohol cause **80 percent** (eighty percent) of attacks, with **triglycerides** (blood fats) over **1000 mg per dL** (one thousand units) and calcium over **10 mg per dL** (ten units) as metabolic triggers needing **same-admission cholecystectomy** (gallbladder out this stay) for biliary cases.

steps.say: Scanning too early misses dead tissue, so the best pictures come after three days. Gas bubbles inside the gland mean infection has set in, and that changes everything about treatment.
steps.tx: Contrast **CT at 72 to 96 hours** (three to four days) stages necrosis and detects gas in **infected necrosis** (infected dead tissue), while early CT underestimates necrosis and stays reserved for diagnostic doubt when the cause stays unclear after basic tests.

vis.alt: Pancreas with blackened necrotic zones, walled-off cavity, fat changes and a scan inset.
vis.caption: Necrotising pancreatitis: pancreatic necrosis with walled-off cavity, fat saponification and scan correlation. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Infected dead tissue is removed from the least invasive route upward. A skin drain comes first, the scope cleans through the stomach next, and keyhole surgery through the flank is the last resort.
steps.tx: **Infected necrosis** (septic dead tissue) with gas or persistent sepsis beyond **4 weeks** (four weeks) follows the **step-up** (escalating ladder) PANTER path from percutaneous drainage through endoscopic **necrosectomy** (scope debridement) to retroperitoneal debridement through a small flank incision as the final rung.

steps.say: Once the dead tissue walls itself off into a mature cavity, a wide metal tube through the stomach wall lets the debris drain inside the gut. Open surgery is avoided in most such cases.
steps.tx: **Walled-off necrosis** (mature dead-tissue cavity) after **4 weeks** (four weeks) with obstruction or infection needs endoscopic **cystgastrostomy** (stomach-to-cavity window) with **lumen-apposing stent** (wide metal tube) rather than open surgery in suitable mature collections with a defined wall around them already.

vis.alt: Endoscope placing a wide metal stent from the stomach into a debris-filled walled cavity.
vis.caption: Walled-off necrosis drainage: transgastric metal stent emptying necrotic debris into the stomach. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A hugely swollen belly can squeeze the kidneys and lungs to failure. Bladder pressure readings warn of this, and draining fluid collections may avert opening the abdomen in some patients.
steps.tx: **Abdominal compartment syndrome** (belly pressure failure) with **bladder pressure** (urine-bag gauge) over **20 mmHg** (twenty units) plus organ failure needs decompressive laparotomy, with percutaneous drainage tried first when drainable collections dominate the picture and no dead bowel exists inside the cavity.

steps.say: Feeding through the gut from the second day keeps the bowel wall alive and blocks germs crossing into the blood. Starving the patient or giving preventive antibiotics does not help and may harm.
steps.tx: **Enteral feeding** (gut feeding) within **48 hours** (two days) through a **nasojejunal** (nose-to-bowel) tube preserves the **gut barrier** (bowel wall defence) and cuts infection, while prophylactic antibiotics and probiotics do not prevent infected necrosis and add no survival benefit in randomised trials.

steps.say: A stone blocking the bile duct with fever and jaundice alongside pancreas inflammation needs the duct opened within a day. Without infection, the duct can wait until the pancreas settles.
steps.tx: Cholangitis with **biliary pancreatitis** (stone-triggered inflammation) needs **urgent ERCP** (emergency duct opening) within **24 hours** (one day), while mere biliary obstruction without cholangitis waits for the attack to settle fully before elective clearance in a planned sitting once fully recovered.
